disposition_reason: Tables 2 and 3 print per-product mean Zn, Pb, Cd and Ca for 23 powdered milks and infant formulas and 32 fluid milks bought in Brasilia.

study.design: Cross-sectional retail survey of 55 infant formulas and milks (22 brand names); one sample per product analysed in triplicate
study.origin: Dairy farms in central-west (Goias), southeast (Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais) and south (Parana, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina) Brazil, plus Argentina (4) and the Netherlands (1), per product labels
study.market: Local supermarkets, Brasilia, Federal District, Brazil
study.method: Closed-vessel microwave digestion (HNO3/H2O2); Zn, Cd, Pb by anodic stripping voltammetry (hanging mercury drop electrode); Ca by flame AAS
study.lod_text: Method LOD; LOQ (digest solution): Zn 1.89; 6.32 ug/L, Pb 2.71; 9.04 ug/L, Cd 0.62; 2.08 ug/L, Ca 0.206; 0.687 mg/L (Table 1)
study.qa: Spike recovery on three infant formulas: Zn 92-93%, Pb 91-111%, Cd 95-100%, Ca 90-110%; repeatability, reproducibility and control charts over eight weeks; no CRM reported

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Brazilian maximum Cd in milk products
FAO/WHO maximum Pb in milk cited by authors
Brazilian maximum Pb, infant formulas / fluid milk
Brazilian maximum Zn cited by authors

unresolved: Abstract gives median powdered Pb 0.109 mg/kg and Cd 0.033 mg/kg and median fluid Pb 0.084 mg/kg; these medians cannot be reproduced from Table 2/3 as printed (for example the powdered Pb median with dashes as zero is 0.1235 mg/kg), so medians were not recorded as findings.
Dash cells in Tables 2 and 3 are undefined in the table footnotes; read as below LOD from the text and Figure 1 caption.
The recovery-test text lists 'known amounts added' to L1-L3 (e.g. L1 0.0037 mg/g Pb) that equal the measured Table 2 values; spike levels are therefore unclear.
Product names in Tables 2 and 3 are brand names; findings use the paper's sample codes (L1-L55) only.

Exceedance statements (62% of samples above FAO/WHO Pb reference; seven infant formulas and 22 fluid samples above Brazilian Pb limits; ten powdered samples above the Brazilian Zn limit) are not recorded as findings.
